Don Madge - South Africa's first UFC Superstar?

By: Julian Sun | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We reveal an intimate portrait in the life of up & coming UFC fighter Don Madge

Unique Selling Point:
MMA is the fastest growing sport in the world thanks to the rise of the UFC. UFC fighters are some of the biggest stars in the world with the likes of Connor Mcgregor & Cris Cyborg regarded as genuine superstars. South African fighters have struggled to crack it in the UFC. South African Don Madge wants to change that as he takes his shot at glory inside the fabled UFC octagon.

Summary:
We reveal an intimate portrait of UFC Fighter Don Madge, an elite athlete, showcasing the desire and dedication required to make it to the top of the fastest growing sport in the world.

Further information:
Mixed Marital Arts or MMA has become the fastest growing sport in the world thanks to the rise of the UFC (or Ultimate Fighting Championship). This is an organisation that was worth just $2million back in 2001. 15 years later it had grown in market value to $3,7 billion. By 2016, this once obscure business delivered $US170 million in profits before interest and tax, and was ranked by Forbes as the world's seventh most valuable sporting brand. It is the largest Pay-Per-View (PPV) event provider globally, broadcasting in more than 163 countries to more than 1.1 billion households in 35 languages. Over this time, the sport has shed its reputation as human cock fighting into a well respected sport that has perhaps eclipsed boxing as the premier contact sport in the world. It is well regulated and has won mainstream appeal leading to the rise of genuine superstars like Connor McGregor & Ronda Rousey.

This year has seen Supersport sign a deal to broadcast UFC across sub-saharan Africa on 2019. I’ve reached out to Supersport to provide a spokesman to comment on why they’ve decided to broadcast the UFC (and also to obtain footage of greatest UFC moments)

Whilst there are many MMA organisations throughout the world (such as South Africa’s own EFC), it is the UFC that is the most prestigious. To make it to the UFC is to make it to the pinnacle of the sport. Over the years several South Africans have been able to win contracts to fight in the UFC with mixed success. Now the latest South African hopeful has been given his shot at glory.

His name is Don Madge and he signed his UFC contract in 2018. Don is a talented Muay Thai fighter who achieved great success with the EFC early on in his career but the step-up to the UFC has presented Don with an opportunity of a lifetime. He won his first fight in October last year and is in training for his next fight in April this year.

Our story will focus on the training and dedication required for Don to achieve success in the UFC. We will shine a spotlight on the training required to become an elite fighter. What are the sacrifices that Don has had to make to make his dreams come true? How does he prepare mentally and physically to fight? What does the life of a professional MMA fighter look like? What support structures are required to excel? How difficult is it to earn a living from being a professional MMA fighter?

To paint this portrait, we will not only interview Don and his trainer Richie Kwan but will also spend a day shooting the training regime that Don follows. We’ll see him in the gym and in the ring. We’ll shoot this in a very stylised manner. Here’s a reference of our treatment: (https://vimeo.com/120420073)

To contextualise how great an achievement it is for Don to win a UFC contract, we’ll speak to journalists and other MMA trainers who can talk to how hard it is to win a UFC contract and how previous South Africans have done.

We’ll also be able to conduct a Skype interview with Cris Cyborg, an American-Brazilian mixed martial artist currently signed with the UFC. She is the former UFC, Strikeforce and Invicta FC World Featherweight Champion. Cris played a crucial role in helping Don secure a contract as he was her sparring partner. This will also show that women participate in the sport. She is regarded as the greatest woman MMA fighter ever.

Finally with Don being hyped as the great South African hope in the UFC, we’ll also interview 2 other young South African MMA fighters who have the potential to make it in the UFC themselves: Roedi Roots & Zuluboy

With this story I am looking to create an intimate portrait of an elite athlete, showcasing the desire and dedication required to make it to the top of the fastest growing sport in the world.

Press Release:


It’s one of the fastest growing sports in the world thanks to the rise of America’s Ultimate Fighting Championship. Mixed martial arts is drawing South African talent to the famed UFC octagon. What will it take for up-and-coming South African fighter Don Madge to make his international mark in 2019?

Script:


INTRO VOICE OVER:

To be a professional mixed martial artist is to know pain

The pain of solitude

The pain of sacrifice

It demands so much

Strength

Stamina

Discipline

Resilience

And Heart

All in pursuit of the ultimate goal:

To become champion


V/O: Where once MMA was thought of as a brutal novelty consigned to the fringes of society, it is now considered the fastest growing sport in the world thanks to the rise of the UFC or Ultimate Fighting Championship.

Worth a mere $2 million back in 2001, it is now valued at a staggering $7 billion.

Today, the UFC is broadcast in 163 countries to more than 1.1 billion households that has turned the likes of Connor McGregor, Jose Aldo and Rhonda Rousey into genuine superstars

Derek Link: It may be violent and bloody but Mixed Martial Arts has erupted as a major spectator sport around the world. Now South Africa’s Don Madge is setting the UFC octagon alight

V/O: Don Madge’s obsession with martial arts began when he was just 6. Although he excelled at traditional sports it was combat sports that held his fascination.

[Don on his love for martial arts, discovering muay thai and telling his parents he wanted to do this for a living]

V/O: A supremely gifted fighter, by the age of 15, he was crowned South African Muay Thai champion. When he finished school, he travelled to Thailand to pursue a professional career.

[Don on going to Thailand]
V/O: Don became a star in Thailand, winning most of his 70 professional fights

When he returned to South Africa in 2011, MMA had exploded in popularity and Don soon made an impression with EFC President Cairo Howarth

[Cairo on Don in the EFC]


V/O: Having won universal acclaim fighting in the EFC, Don yearned for the ultimate prize, one that has eluded all South African MMA fighters to date: Success in the UFC

Derek Links to Richie


[comments from Richie & Don about training and attaining success]


V/O: All over the world, It’s every fighter’s dream to make it to the UFC. Don’s big break came when he was contacted by Cris Cyborg to be her training partner. She is considered by many to be one of the finest female mixed-martial artists in the history of the sport.

“She was looking for a tall left handed southpaw to train with”

Kris was so impressed with Don’s ability that she recommended to the UFC that they sign him.


Don comments on signing to UFC
V/O: The result was Don putting pen to paper in April last year. At the age of 28 and in the prime of his career, he stepped into the fabled octagon for the first time in October at UFC Fight Night 138 in Moncton Canada


Comments from Don & Richie about fight

V/O: A keen observer of the fight was Alastair Bishop, host of a popular MMA podcast here in South Africa

[Comments for Alastair]
V/O: Apart from hardcore MMA fans like Alastair, the majority of South Africa weren’t able to witness Don’s spectacular UFC debut.

But now thanks to an exciting new partnership with Supersport, fight fans will be able to follow Don’s career along with all their favourite UFC stars as CEO Gideon Khobane explains

[comment from Gideon]

V/O: Don represents the second generation of local fighters looking to conquer the UFC.

To date there has never been a South African champion.

So does Don have what it takes to become this country’s first UFC superstar?

[comments about Don’s potential]


V/O: Don’s singular ambition that he’s had since he was a young boy remains undimmed – to be the ultimate fighting champion.
